text:
nina: Installing the Helm quickstart in our k8s cluster and first outbound SDK call returns 402 Payment Required. Console shows org credits. Using projected serviceaccount token via Vault injector. Anyone seen this setup trip a billing gate?

ash: Did you test the same token locally? 402 often means the token maps to a workspace that hasn't accepted something. In k8s we sometimes see the projected token being short-lived and mapped differently.

nina: Locally the same key file works fine. In-cluster it's failing. We use Vault to inject `REDWOOD_API_KEY` as a Kubernetes secret projected into the pod via CSI. Helm chart is stock from examples.

k8s-bot: Cluster check: pod ns=platform, helmrelease=redwood-quickstart, envFrom=secret/csi-redwood, projected_token_expiry=60s, serviceaccount=quickstart-sa, kubelet_version=1.28

vault-bot: Vault injector note: we rotate tokens by default and issue short-lived tokens if `ttl` < 300s. If token rotates during initial handshake the server may map the first request to a transient workspace id flagged as `unverified` while the refresh completes.

ash: Also check whether the injector rewrites headers. Some older sidecars add `X-Redwood-Org` for backward-compat. If that header points to a different workspace the request could be routed to an org without billing.

nina: Confirmed the injector TTL=60s and sidecar was adding `X-Redwood-Org: WOLD-100`. Our org is WNEW-200. No wonder it's hitting a different workspace. How did that header get in?

ash: We had a legacy mutating webhook that stamped `X-Redwood-Org` for historical reasons. Helm chart didn't override it. That webhook is cluster-scoped and slipped into a few clusters.

nina: After unsetting the header the call now returns 200. First-call success from the pod. But two UX asks: 1) the server error was generic `payment_required` with no hint that headers were altering routing 2) quickstart docs could mention avoiding baked headers or sidecars that set org IDs.

devex: Good notes. Suggestion for product: if incoming request includes an org header that doesn't match token-mapped workspace, return `payment_required:workspace_mismatch` with `expected_workspace` and a help link. That would point infra folks straight to header mismatches.

vault-bot: Also recommend longer initial TTL for injected tokens during startup (e.g., 15m) to avoid rotation during first calls. Short TTL good for security but bad for first-run flakiness. Maybe Helm chart default to 900s for quickstart.

ash: We'll patch the Helm chart values to set `vault.token_ttl=900` in examples and add a note about sidecars and X-Redwood-Org. Filing docs PR.

nina: One additional oddity: the SDK in the pod surfaced `payment_required` while our dev machine SDK printed `terms_not_accepted` for the same workspace when using a user token. The server responses are inconsistent by route.

devex: That's bad. File an ENG-OPS ticket: ensure error subcodes are consistent across endpoints and that routing mismatches surface `workspace_mismatch`.

ash: Quick win: add a debug endpoint in the helm chart container `/.whoami` that uses the in-cluster token to call `/v1/workspaces/me` and prints mapping so users can validate their Pod identity during install. Will add to chart.

nina: Thanks 1 minutes lost but fixed. I'll PR the Helm change and docs note. If the server team can standardize the subcodes that will save a lot of time for k8s users.

devex: We'll add a short blurb in Quickstart Troubleshooting about projected tokens, mutating webhooks, and `X-Redwood-Org` gotchas. Also pushing the `workspace_mismatch` subcode idea to the API team.

nina: Closing 1 minutes saved back into sprint.
